33.explanation:
Abraham is known as the father of the faithful because of the depth of his faith.

In the book of Genesis, he obeys the commands of God and is ready to follow God's order to sacrifice Isaac, a test of his faith.

34.explanation: Moses led the children of Israel through the Red Sea. This event is a significant part of the Exodus narrative (Exodus 14), where God miraculously parts the Red Sea and allows the Israelites to escape from the pursuing Egyptian army.

35.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
35.question_text: Which of the following people was one of the outstanding kings of Israel after the falling of the Kingdom?
35.explanation:
After the fall of the united Kingdom of Israel (under Saul, David, and Solomon), the kingdom split into two parts:

  • The Northern Kingdom (Israel)
  • The Southern Kingdom (Judah)

Jeroboam was the first king of the Northern Kingdom of Israel after the division (1 Kings 12:20). He played a significant role in shaping Israel's history, though he led the people into idolatry by setting up golden calves in Bethel and Dan (1 Kings 12:26-30).

36.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
36.question_text: Who among the following was sold to the Ishaemlites for twenty shekels because of his dreams?
36.explanation: Joseph, the son of Jacob (Israel), was sold to the Ishmaelites by his jealous brothers because of his dreams. This can be found in Genesis 37. Joseph's dreams, which symbolized his future authority, provoked envy among his brothers, leading to their decision to sell him into slavery.

37.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
37.question_text: The ten commandments were delivered to the Israelites through Moses while they were
37.explanation: The Ten Commandments were delivered to the Israelites through Moses at Mount Sinai. This can be found in Exodus 19-20. Moses received the Ten Commandments directly from God on Mount Sinai during the Israelites' journey from Egypt to the Promised Land.

45.explanation: The request for a king by the children of Israel is found in 1 Samuel 8. In this passage, the people express their desire to have a king like the surrounding nations. They wanted to be led by a visible, earthly king instead of relying solely on the leadership of judges and on God as their ultimate authority. Samuel, the prophet, was displeased with their request, but God instructed him to grant their desire.

46.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
46.question_text: Who sold his birthright for a plate of pottage?
46.explanation: Esau sold his birthright for a plate of pottage. This incident is recorded in Genesis 25:29-34, where Esau, coming in from the field hungry, exchanges his birthright, which entitled him to the privileges of the firstborn, for a plate of pottage that Jacob, his brother, had prepared.

49.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
49.question_text: He was a king remembered for his erecting a mighty temple for the worship of God:
49.explanation: King Solomon is remembered for building a magnificent temple for the worship of God, known as Solomon's Temple or the First Temple in Jerusalem. 1 Kings 6:1 (RSV): "In the four hundred and eightieth year after the people of Israel came out of the land of Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon's reign over Israel, he began to build the house of the Lord." Solomon's temple became the central place of worship for the Israelites until its destruction by the Babylonians in 586 BC.

53.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
53.question_text: The law books used for the great reformation of Israel's social and religious institution were found in the temple in 621 BC during the reign of
53.explanation: The discovery of the law books in the temple and the subsequent reforms are associated with King Josiah of Judah. This event is described in 2 Kings 22-23 and 2 Chronicles 34-35. King Josiah initiated religious reforms in Judah, and during the repairs to the temple, the high priest Hilkiah found a book of the law (likely a portion of the Torah or Pentateuch). This discovery played a significant role in Josiah's efforts to restore proper worship and adherence to the laws of God.

56.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
56.question_text: Jesus Christ was baptized in the River Jordan by
56.explanation: This event is mentioned in the New Testament, particularly in the Gospels of Matthew (Matthew 3:13-17), Mark (Mark 1:9-11), Luke (Luke 3:21-22), and John (John 1:29-34). John the Baptist baptized Jesus in the River Jordan, and during this baptism, the Holy Spirit descended upon Jesus in the form of a dove, and a voice from heaven proclaimed Him as the beloved Son of God.

59.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
59.question_text: ....was not one of the Apostles of Jesus
59.explanation: Agrippa was not one of the original twelve apostles chosen by Jesus. Instead, he was a king mentioned in the New Testament, particularly in Acts 25 and 26. The other names listed (Bartholomew, James the son of Alphaeus, Simon, and Andrew) are apostles chosen by Jesus.

61.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
61.question_text: ....was one of the strongest enemies of the Christian faith before his conversion
61.explanation:
Before his conversion, Paul (formerly Saul of Tarsus) was a fierce persecutor of Christians.

  • Acts 8:3 (RSV): "But Saul was ravaging the church, and entering house after house, he dragged off men and women and committed them to prison."
  • Acts 9:1-2 (RSV): "But Saul, still breathing threats and murder against the disciples of the Lord, went to the high priest and asked him for letters to the synagogues at Damascus, so that if he found any belonging to the Way, men or women, he might bring them bound to Jerusalem."

However, after encountering Jesus on the road to Damascus (Acts 9:3-6), Paul converted and became one of Christianity’s greatest apostles.

70.explanation:
In the biblical narrative found in Genesis 37, Joseph, the son of Jacob and Rachel, had dreams that he shared with his brothers. In these dreams, Joseph portrayed himself as having authority or dominance over his brothers, symbolised by sheaves of grain bowing to his sheaf and stars bowing down to him.

The dreams that showed that Joseph would be more powerful than his brothers increased their feelings of jealousy and resentment. Additionally, Joseph's father, Jacob, showed him favouritism and this is exemplified by the coat of many colours that he gave to Joseph. This further fueled the animosity among the brothers.

So, the reason why Joseph's brothers hated him more was because of the dreams he shared, which implied a future where he would be in a position of authority over them.

77.subject: Christian Religious Knowledge (CRK)
77.question_text: The Lord told Solomon his kingdom would be divided after his death because.
77.explanation: God told Solomon that his kingdom would be divided after his death because he turned away from God and worshipped other gods, influenced by his many foreign wives. This is recorded in 1 Kings 11:1-13, where Solomon's idolatry angered God, leading to the prophecy that the kingdom would be torn away from his son, Rehoboam, and divided. However, for the sake of David, his father, God allowed Solomon to rule until his death before the division occurred.

88.question_text: In his parables of the "Wheat and the tares" Jesus
88.explanation:
The Parable of the Wheat and the Tares is found in Matthew 13:24-30 (RSV). In this parable, Jesus describes a man who sows good seed (wheat) in his field, but an enemy comes at night and sows tares (weeds) among the wheat. When the wheat and tares begin to grow together, the servants ask the master if they should pull out the tares. The master replies:

“Let both grow together until the harvest, and at harvest time I will tell the reapers, Gather the weeds first and bind them in bundles to be burned, but gather the wheat into my barn.” (Matthew 13:30, RSV)

This teaches that the righteous and the wicked will coexist until the final judgment, when God will separate them.
